newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA WANTS TO LIST MORE AIRLINES - NEWSPAPER.
newsitem.headline: CHINA WANTS TO LIST MORE AIRLINES - NEWSPAPER.

text.p: China plans to push more civil aviation firms to go public at home or abroad to raise funds to support one of its fastest-growing transport industries, the China Daily said on Monday.

"We expect a block of China civil aviation shares, including aviation firms and airports, can be formed in domestic and overseas stock markets in the coming years," the newspaper quoted Xia Xinghua, a senior official of the Civil Aviation Administration of China, as saying.
Xia said the recent successful listing of China Southern Airlines Co Ltd in Hong Kong demonstrated foreign investors' keen interest in China's civil aviation market.
China's aviation industry, with annual growth expected to average 15 percent between 1996 and 2000, must seek funds from the equity market to finance future development, Xia said.

Infrastructure development in China's aviation industry, which will include construction of more than 41 airports and the improvement of related facilities, was expected to absorb about 100 billion yuan ($12 billion) by 2000, the newspaper said.
Xia said most Chinese civil aviation enterprises were operating on high assets-to-liabilities ratios, which could be decreased by proceeds from stock issues.
Foreign listing could breathe new life into the aviation industry because it would introduce more advanced managerial know-how and competition, the newspaper said.
Recently-listed Hainan Airlines Co Ltd, which is linked to U.S. financier George Soros, is China's only domestically listed airline.
